===ListClients===
package net.officefloor.hq.app;

import java.util.List;
import net.officefloor.web.ObjectResponse;

/**
 * GET /api/clients — every client the user still works with, in id order, as the list the front-end
 * renders. Archived (tucked-away) clients are retained but excluded here, so they drop off both the
 * list and the search (which filters the same list) without being lost.
 * Wired by officefloor/rest/api/clients.GET.yml.
 */
public class ListClients {

    public void service(ClientRepository clients, ObjectResponse<List<ClientView>> response) {
        List<ClientView> view = clients.findAll().stream()
                .filter(client -> !client.isArchived())
                .sorted((a, b) -> Long.compare(a.getId(), b.getId()))
                .map(ClientView::of)
                .toList();
        response.send(view);
    }
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# The agent's test loop (DESIGN.md §15): build, start the whole app, run ONLY the specs currently

export BASE_URL="http://localhost:${PORT}"

bin/build
bin/start

The test passes. The full build (`bin/build` compiles the front-end and server) succeeded and the acceptance spec is green.

## Summary

I implemented "top five clients on the home screen, ranked by how much they owe" as a small additive full-stack change.

**Server (OfficeFloor REST):**
- `GetTopClients.java` — new logic class. For each non-archived client it sums the due balance across every invoice their projects hold (`invoice.getTotal()` minus payments) — the exact derivation `GetClientStatement` already uses for "how much a client owes" — then ranks by amount descending (ties broken by client id), drops clients owing nothing, and caps at five.
- `DashboardTopClientView.java` — the `{clientId, name, amount}` response record.
- `officefloor/rest/api/dashboard/top-clients.GET.yml` — wires `GET /api/dashboard/top-clients` (under `/api/` so it bypasses the SPA fallback).

**Front-end (additive, new files):**
- `slots/defs/dashboardMain.ts` — declares the `dashboard.main` region (it didn't exist yet).
- `routes/dashboard.tsx` — one-line render of `<DashboardMain.Slot />` to introduce the region on the page.
- `features/dashboard/topClientsApi.ts` — `useQuery` data under key `['dashboard', 'top-clients']` (nested under the shared `['dashboard']` handle so existing invalidations refresh it).
- `features/dashboard/TopClients.tsx` + `topClients.slot.tsx` — the ranked panel filling the region, exposing `data-testid` anchors `dashboard-top-clients`, `top-client-row-<id>`, `top-client-name`, `top-client-amount` (amounts via the shared `formatMoney`).

No schema change was required (all tables already exist), so no Flyway migration was added, and the feature has no audited side effects.
